title: EMAR: Efficient Multi-domain Adaptive Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2602.14960v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Neural retrieval systems are increasingly deployed in multi-domain settings, where each domain may have its own vocabulary and word distribution. A common approach is to fine-tune separate models for each domain, achieving strong in-domain performance while increasing training costs and storage requirements. In contrast, a single model trained jointly across domains avoids model duplication but weakens robustness under domain shift. This creates a trade-off between effectiveness and resource-efficiency. To address this issue, we propose EMAR, a retrieval system that employs a single frozen model shared across all domains and introduces lightweight domain-specific adapters. At inference time, a learned routing mechanism dynamically selects the most suitable adapter for each query. translated_title: EMAR：高效的多领域自适应检索
translated_abstract: 神经检索系统越来越多地被部署在多领域场景中，其中每个领域可能拥有自己的词汇表和词分布。一种常见的做法是为每个领域微调单独的模型，这虽然能在领域内取得出色的性能，但同时增加了训练成本和存储需求。相比之下，跨领域联合训练的单一模型虽然避免了模型重复，却削弱了在领域偏移情况下的鲁棒性。这在效果与资源效率之间造成了权衡。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了EMAR——一个采用跨所有领域共享的单一冻结模型的检索系统，并引入轻量级的领域特定适配器。在推理阶段，一个学习得到的路由机制会动态地为每个查询选择最合适的适配器。EMAR通过在多个领域之间共享计算开销高昂的骨干网络，且无需维护多个模型副本，实现了高效的领域特定检索。
tldr: EMAR提出了一种高效的多领域自适应检索系统，通过共享单一冻结骨干模型、轻量级领域特定适配器以及动态路由机制，在保持强领域内检索效果的同时显著降低了训练成本与存储需求。
en_tdlr: EMAR is an efficient multi-domain adaptive retrieval system that shares a single frozen backbone across domains, uses lightweight domain-specific adapters with a learned routing mechanism, and achieves strong domain-specific performance while greatly reducing training costs and storage requirements.
